land.text: Zabid, taken by Turan-Shah's Ayyubid troops on 13 May 1174, and the Mahdid lands

successors.note: Cliopatria's Ayyubid Sultanate begins in 1177; the Ayyubid dossier of this group starts in 1171. Turan-Shah took Aden "later that year" and Sana'a in 1175 (Turan-Shah page).

capitals.name: Zabid
capitals.note: Zabid was the Najahid capital and the Mahdids' seat: "the Mahdids took over Zabid in 1158" (Zabid page); the Mahdids page calls it a city taken, not an official capital.

rulers.name: Ali bin Mahdi
rulers.note: Page: "established himself in the city but died soon after, in 1159"; the Najahids page has him killing the last Najahid in 1158.

rulers.name: Mahdi bin Ali
rulers.note: The page gives his death in 1163 only.

rulers.name: Abd an-Nabi bin Ali
rulers.note: Took full control in 1163; Zabid fell on 13 May 1174; he and his brother Ahmad "were strangulated in 1176".

correction.text: the Mahdid state as in mahdids_1164 (the Tihama with Ta'izz and Ibb), for 1169-1174: Cliopatria's row 'Mahdids' for these years is the Oman shape of the Nabhani dynasty, which this dossier does not draw

keyframe_review.note: 84 k km2 for 1169-1235 in the interior of Oman (55.5-59.9 E, 21.3-26.3 N), nothing to do with Zabid and the Tihama. The five Oman shapes of this Cliopatria row (84 k km2 in the interior of Oman, 4.4 k km2 from 1475) are the Nabhani dynasty of Oman: the Nabhani page gives "Country: Oman (historical)", founded 1154 and dissolved 1624 and says they "ruled [Oman] as hereditary kings (muluk) from 1154 until 1624". They are reviewed there (nabhani-dynasty) as new keyframes. Do not draw it under the Mahdids. Fix fx-31 (F182): the correction used to be the Oman shape itself ({'cliopatria': 'Mahdids', 'year': 1169}), so the compiler drew the Nabhani's 346 Oman cells under the Mahdids in 1169-1174 and the pair conflicted (692 cell-years, won by mahdids by the size rule). The shape to use instead is now the Mahdid state of mahdids_1164, which has no cell in common with the Oman shape. The Nabhani dynasty page (opened 2026-11-01) has 'Country: Oman (historical)', founded 1154, dissolved 1624 and no mention of Yemen, Zabid, Ta'izz or Ibb; the Mahdids page (same date) has Ta'izz and Ibb falling in 1164, Zabid taken on 13 May 1174 and no mention of Oman. The later 'wrong' keyframes (1236-1502) lie after the end of the state in 1174 and are not drawn.

correction.text: Zabid and the central Tihama round it

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the Mahdid state at its birth, 1158-1163: Zabid and the Tihama round it. The Mahdids page has Ali "propagated his religious ideas in the Tihama lowland" and his sons "consolidated the power relations in the Tihama"; the page gives no extent or area figure ("It gives no area or extent figures"), so the radius is a reading. The Turan-Shah page says Yemen was "previously divided into three states (Sana'a, Zabid, and Aden)".

correction.text: the Tihama with Ta'izz and Ibb, the Mahdid state of Abd an-Nabi

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1164-1174: the Tihama (the Sulaymanid north of it annexed under Abd an-Nabi, undated) plus Ta'izz and Ibb, which "fell in 1164" while Aden was besieged. The page does not name the conqueror of Ta'izz and Ibb in that sentence, only that Abd an-Nabi pursued an expansive policy; the Mahdids also raided Lahij and Abyan "for plunder" (undated). The 1173 defeat by the Zurayids and the Hamdanid sultan of Sana'a is not shown as a loss of land (Abd an-Nabi "withdrew to Zabid"). Cliopatria's all-Yemen shape (212 k km2, row "Nabhani Dynasty") is far too large for this state.

region.text: Zabid and the central Tihama round it

ledger.note: 1158: Ali ibn Mahdi's followers take Zabid and end the Najahid dynasty. "With this event, the slave dynasty came an end and the Mahdids took over Zabid in 1158"; "the Mahdids (1158 to 1174)". The Najahids page: "Their last sovereign was killed by Ali ibn Mahdi the Kharijite in 1158"; the Mahdids page dates Ali's establishment in the city to 1159.

1164: Ta'izz and Ibb fall to the Mahdids under Abd an-Nabi while Aden is besieged. "The cities Ta'izz and Ibb fell in 1164 and Aden was besieged in the same year." The sentence does not name the attacker, the preceding one credits Abd an-Nabi's expansive policy; the defenders are not named.

region.text: Zabid and the central Tihama round it

ledger.note: 1174: Turan-Shah's Ayyubid army takes Zabid on 13 May. "The Ayyubid troops quickly overran the bulk of Yemen and took Zabid on 13 May 1174"; the city was looted and Abd an-Nabi and his brother Ahmad were taken prisoner. The Turan-Shah page: "Turanshah set out in 1174 and quickly conquered the town of Zabid in May."

region.text: the Tihama with Ta'izz and Ibb

ledger.note: 1174: the Mahdid state ends. "Both of them were strangulated in 1176 ... probably due to an attempt to revive Mahdid rule, and with them the brief era of the Mahdids came to an end." The rest of the state (the Tihama, Ta'izz and Ibb) is not itemised by the pages; "the bulk of Yemen" was overrun in 1174.

wars.name: Mahdid conquest of the Najahid Tihama

zones.text: Zabid and the central Tihama round it

wars.outcome: Ali bin Mahdi attacked his former hosts in 1143 (the attempt on al-Kadra failed); war broke out again in 1150; Surur al-Fatik was murdered in 1156; the last Najahid ruler was killed in 1158 and Ali established himself in Zabid, dying in 1159.
wars.note: The Najahids page names a Mahdid envoy killing Surur in a Zabid mosque in 551 AH (1156) and the last sovereign killed in 1158.

wars.name: Mahdid siege of Aden
wars.outcome: Ta'izz and Ibb fell and Aden was besieged in 1164; "An advantageous peace was concluded with the Zurayids of Aden."
wars.note: The page does not name the besieger of Aden in that sentence.

wars.name: Zurayid and Hamdanid war against the Mahdids
wars.outcome: The Zurayids of Aden allied with the Hamdanid sultan of Sana'a in 1172 and "Together they managed to defeat the Mahdid forces in 1173"; Abd an-Nabi withdrew to Zabid. No loss of land is named.

wars.name: Ayyubid conquest of Yemen

zones.text: Zabid and the central Tihama round it

wars.outcome: Turan-Shah set out in 1174 and took Zabid in May (13 May 1174), Aden later that year and drove the Hamdanid sultan Ali ibn Hatim out of Sana'a in 1175; Abd an-Nabi and Ahmad were strangled in 1176.

certainty.note: A city state with a lowland and two highland towns; no page gives a frontier.

notes: Mahdids. Five pages opened (budget 5). CLIOPATRIA ROW SWAPPED: the row named "Mahdids" (1169-1506, five shapes) lies in the interior of Oman and matches the Nabhani dynasty of Oman (1154-1624, Nabhani page), while the row named "Nabhani Dynasty" (1169-1176, one shape of 212 k km2, 42.2-49.5 E, 12.6-18.6 N) lies in Yemen and matches the Mahdids of Zabid (1158-1174; the Mahdids page: "briefly held power in the period between 1159 and 1174"). This dossier is the Mahdids of Zabid, as the Wikipedia title Mahdids and Wikidata Q1884830 say; the five Oman shapes are marked wrong and are reviewed in the nabhani-dynasty dossier. The Yemen shape (nabhani-dynasty_1169) is reviewed there as wrong for the Nabhanis; for the Mahdids it is far too large: the Turan-Shah page says Yemen was "divided into three states (Sana'a, Zabid, and Aden)", so the new keyframes are built from the pages (Tihama, Ta'izz, Ibb), not from Cliopatria. Start 1158 (Zabid and Najahids pages; the Najahid dossier of group me-08 ends the Najahids in 1158 with counterpart mahdids) against 1159 on the Mahdids page. End: Zabid fell on 13 May 1174 (Mahdids page; the Turan-Shah page says only "May"); the last Mahdids were executed in 1176. Not settled: the extent of the state (no page gives area or boundary), who held Ta'izz and Ibb in 1164, the date of the annexation of the Sulaymanid north Tihama, the Lahij and Abyan raids. Counterparts needing dossiers: hamdanids-of-sanaa (the sultanate of Sana'a, 1172-1175; also noted in the Zurayid dossier). Gazetteer: Zabid is {"place": "Zabīd"}; Ta'izz is spelled "Ta`izz" as in Natural Earth.
